title: Access token accepted by the resource server after logout
vulnerable_behaviour: RP-initiated logout ends the IdP session but leaves the access and refresh tokens bound to that session valid; introspection still reports active=true.
fixed_behaviour: Session termination marks every access and refresh token bound to the session as revoked.
termination_trigger: explicit federated logout: GET RP1 /logout -> GET IdP /logout?id_token_hint (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0)
declared_expected_scope: all tokens bound to the IdP session
protected_operation: GET RS /api/data with the pre-logout Bearer access token (validated by RFC 7662 introspection)
cwe_rule_path: termination trigger present (RP-initiated logout at the IdP)
artifact presented after the trigger (Bearer token)
=> explicit-termination failure: token lifetime not bound to the session it was issued under

neighbour_rules.CWE-613 original sense (time-only expira: not matched: the token is still within its 600 s lifetime but an explicit trigger occurred

uncertainty.reason: the introspection step in the trace shows active=true after the IdP reported logged_out=true

lifecycle_event: explicit federated logout: GET RP1 /logout -> GET IdP /logout?id_token_hint (RP-Initiated Logout 1.0)
normative_basis: Declared laboratory scope for RP-initiated logout; not a universal claim that every RP logout must revoke every access token.
